package_info.why_malicious: Apache Struts 2 is vulnerable because its framework architecture allows user-supplied input to be evaluated as OGNL expressions. This enables attackers to inject and execute arbitrary code if an injection point is present. Multiple vulnerabilities have allowed attackers to bypass OGNL security controls, manipulate application state, and execute system commands, resulting in remote code execution and privilege escalation.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when user input is processed by a vulnerable endpoint
execution_context.file_location: Framework internals (such as error message handling or user input evaluation logic)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when user input is evaluated by the OGNL engine, the code enables static method access and executes an operating system command via Java Runtime, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code allows user input to alter OGNL security settings and execute system commands, which should never be possible in a secure application.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal OGNL evaluation is restricted to safe expressions for data binding; it should not allow user input to enable static method access or execute arbitrary commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for user-controlled static method access or command execution in OGNL expressions.
key_indicators: Dynamically enables static method access via user input
Executes system command using Java Runtime from OGNL expression

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when user input is processed by a vulnerable endpoint
execution_context.file_location: Framework internals (such as error message handling or user input evaluation logic)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when user input is evaluated by the OGNL engine, the code creates a new ProcessBuilder object and starts a new process to execute an OS command, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: User input should not be able to instantiate system-level objects or spawn new processes, as this enables attackers to execute arbitrary commands.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal OGNL evaluation should restrict object instantiation and process creation from user input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for user-controlled process creation via OGNL expressions.
key_indicators: Executes arbitrary system command through OGNL

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when user input is processed by a vulnerable endpoint
execution_context.file_location: Framework internals (such as error message handling or user input evaluation logic)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when user input is evaluated by the OGNL engine, the code resets the OGNL security context to default (removing restrictions) and executes an OS command, enabling arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bypassing the OGNL security context and executing system commands from user input is a clear sign of exploitation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal OGNL evaluation enforces security restrictions to prevent arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for resetting the OGNL security context from user input.
key_indicators: Resets OGNL security context to default
Executes system command via Java Runtime

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when user input is processed by a vulnerable endpoint
execution_context.file_location: Framework internals (such as error message handling or user input evaluation logic)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when user input is evaluated by the OGNL engine, the code clears OGNL security blacklists, resets member access, and executes an OS command, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Clearing OGNL security blacklists and executing system commands from user input demonstrates a deliberate attempt to bypass security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Security blacklists should remain immutable and not be alterable by user input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for clearing OGNL security blacklists via user input.

execution_context.file_location: Framework internals (such as error message handling or user input evaluation logic)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when user input is evaluated by the OGNL engine, the code uses alternate object paths to clear OGNL security blacklists and then executes an OS command, enabling arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Using alternate object paths to bypass OGNL security controls and execute system commands is a sophisticated exploitation technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: User input should not be able to alter OGNL security settings or execute code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for this behavior in production code.
key_indicators: Uses alternate object paths to access OGNL internals

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when user input is passed to getText() in application code
execution_context.file_location: Application code (e.g., user input passed to getText() method)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when user input is passed to getText(), the code evaluates the input as an OGNL expression, allowing manipulation of non-blacklisted object properties (such as setting isAdmin to true), resulting in privilege escalation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Evaluating user input as an OGNL expression allows attackers to manipulate application state or escalate privileges by setting sensitive object properties.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: User input should be treated as data, not as code to be evaluated by OGNL.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve safe evaluation of trusted expressions, not direct evaluation of untrusted user input.
key_indicators: Evaluates user input as OGNL expression
Allows manipulation of application state or object properties

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies an injection point where user input is evaluated as an OGNL expression.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to inject arbitrary OGNL payloads

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts OGNL payloads to bypass security mechanisms, such as clearing blacklists or resetting member access.
Attacker executes arbitrary system commands via OGNL expressions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution or privilege escalation

attack_chain.action: Attacker manipulates application state, such as setting the isAdmin property to true, for privilege escalation.

behavioral_signatures: Evaluation of user input as OGNL expressions at runtime
Dynamic modification of OGNL security settings, such as allowStaticMethodAccess or memberAccess, from user input
Instantiation of system-level objects (e.g., ProcessBuilder, Runtime) via OGNL expressions controlled by user input
Clearing or modifying OGNL security blacklists (excludedClasses, excludedPackageNames) at runtime
file_indicators: Custom error message handling code that evaluates user input as OGNL
Application code that passes user input to getText(), findValue(), or other OGNL evaluation methods
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound connections from the application server, especially if attacker payloads include network exfiltration
Unusual process creation events, such as spawning cmd.exe, calc.exe, or other binaries from the application server
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application code paths where user input is evaluated as OGNL expressions. Use static analysis to identify injection points, such as calls to getText() or findValue() with user input. Monitor for dynamic changes to OGNL security settings or instantiation of system-level objects from OGNL expressions. Implement runtime monitoring to detect suspicious process creation or outbound network activity originating from the application server.
